title.narrative: Faith-Led Emergency Response to Ebola and Displacement in North Kivu (EAC)

description.narrative: The resurgence of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in mid-May 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo is occurring within a context of ongoing conflict, displacement, and limited access to basic services. In North Kivu, particularly in Beni, Oicha, Lubero-South, Rutshuru, and Goma, these combined risks have increased vulnerabilities, with displaced populations living in overcrowded conditions and exposed to infectious diseases, including Ebola. Living conditions are marked by poor access to water, sanitation, and healthcare, while weak community awareness and trust continue to hinder effective prevention. At the same time, households have lost livelihoods, host communities face increasing pressure, and women and children are exposed to protection risks. These factors contribute to the continued spread of Ebola and limit the effectiveness of response efforts. In response, the Eglise Anglicane du Congo (EAC) will implement a community-based intervention focused on Ebola prevention and control. The project will prioritise training of religious leaders, community actors, and volunteers on prevention measures, early detection, and referral mechanisms. EAC will conduct large-scale sensitisation campaigns through churches, markets, schools, and public spaces, complemented by door-to-door outreach targeting vulnerable and displaced populations. These activities will be reinforced through the production and dissemination of communication materials, including posters, leaflets, and radio messages in local languages. The project will also address misinformation through community dialogue and interactive radio programmes to strengthen trust and promote behaviour change. In parallel, essential hygiene and prevention materials—such as handwashing facilities, soap, chlorine, thermometers, and basic protective equipment—will be distributed to community structures, churches, and health facilities. Leveraging its church network, EAC will mobilise local leaders to promote safe practices and strengthen community alert systems. Coordination with health authorities and partners will ensure alignment with the national response, while continuous monitoring and community feedback mechanisms will support accountability.
